name: Relativistic slingshot gain dv = 2U/(1+U^2) (strong-field limit; Einstein velocity addition of 2U) and its time symmetry

published_statement: Tree (arrival.py:7-9): 'REVERSE SLINGSHOT. The coupling is time-symmetric: a pass with the deflector receding takes back exactly what a head-on pass gave, dv = 2U/(1+U^2) either way.' arrival.py:37: 'dv = 2U/(1+U^2), the strong-field limit. Sign is the encounter geometry.' arrival.py:109-111: 'dv = 2U/(1+U^2) with the deflector approaching; the same magnitude negative with it receding. Braking is departure run backwards and costs nothing.' External content that could be read: Zhang (2020) p.13 says head-tail encounters decelerate, and that aberration makes head-on encounters statistically commoner. The optimised upper limit is 'a 50% gain [in gamma] when |v_A| = 0.2c'. The Newtonian analogue in Acevedo & Ritz (2026) Eq. (2.10) is Delta eps = u_M2 v_i (cos beta - cos(beta+chi)), 'maximal energy gain is 2 u_M2 v_i, which occurs when beta = 0 and chi = 180 deg'. That formula is 'technically only valid for the restricted 3-body problem, in which the heavy component is effectively at rest and a sufficiently close encounter ... can be described as a two-body hyperbolic scattering event in the rest frame of the secondary'. The exact law re-derived here: a full reversal (deflection pi) in the rest frame of a deflector moving at U adds exactly 2 artanh U to the ship's rapidity. From rest this gives v_f = 2U/(1+U^2).
published_hypotheses: Elastic scattering in the deflector's rest frame: the speed at infinity is conserved there. This needs a stationary, asymptotically flat field in that frame, i.e. an isolated deflector moving uniformly during the encounter (restricted-3-body idealisation; Acevedo & Ritz Sec. 2).
Test particle: the ship's mass is negligible against the deflector's, so recoil is neglected (Acevedo & Ritz p.5: energy absorbed by M2 'scales as m_chi/M2 and is therefore negligible').
Maximum gain needs the head-on geometry (beta = 0) and full reversal (chi = 180 deg) (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Deflection near pi without striking the body needs a compact deflector, which is the strong-field clause (Zhang abstract, p.1).

The single-encounter formula holds when one hyperbolic encounter describes the event. In compact equal-mass BH binaries, where spheres of influence overlap, ejections exceed it by an order-unity factor (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Zhang's 50%-per-pass figure is optimised over the entry phase phi0 and the angular momentum L (Fig. 8 caption, p.13-14).
Special-relativistic velocity addition between the deflector frame and the lab frame (Einstein 1905; NAMED-NOT-READ; re-derived here).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, arrival.py:7-9, 36-39, 109-111: 'either way' / 'the same magnitude negative with it receding' holds as a VELOCITY change only when the incoming speed is exactly w = 2U/(1+U^2), the exact time reverse of a from-rest departure. The general law is in rapidity. Head-on: theta_f = theta_w + 2 artanh U. Tail-on (1D full reversal): theta_f = 2 artanh U - theta_w. Counterexample to the unconditioned reading: at w = 0.866, U = 0.35 the speed falls by 0.3390, not 0.6236, and the ship ends at -0.5270 c, moving backwards (rederive D). slingshot_dv(U, head_on=False) takes no incoming-speed argument, so it silently encodes this condition.

DROPPED, arrival.py:36-39 docstring: 'ship initially at rest in the frame where the deflector moves at U'. The formula is Einstein addition of U twice FROM REST. Speeds from successive passes do not add; only rapidities do.

DROPPED, arrival.py:160 ('0.87 c -- reverse slingshot IF the destination has a deflector'): one reverse pass stops 0.866 c only if the deflector recedes at U = 0.577316 c. At U = 0.35 c braking needs 1.802 passes, at 0.20 c 3.248, at 0.10 c 6.562 and at 0.04 c 16.45 (rederive F). Each full-reversal pass flips the ship's direction, so multi-pass braking also needs the destination binary to return the ship between passes and every pass to be steered. None of this is stated at the owner.

DROPPED (never named in the tree), arrival.py:7-10, 108-117: an isolated, unaccelerated deflector during the encounter, i.e. the restricted-3-body idealisation. In a binary the deflector accelerates and the companion's field is present. Acevedo & Ritz (2603.08781 p.5) find that in compact equal-mass BH binaries the single-encounter formula fails by an order-unity factor. Time reversal of a trajectory through a binary maps it to a trajectory through the time-reversed (counter-orbiting) binary. So 'takes back exactly' in a real binary needs the destination configuration to be the time-reversed image of the departure, and the single-encounter law does not guarantee that.

DROPPED (never named in the tree): test-particle limit and no radiation reaction. The exact finite-mass result is 2V/(1+V^2) with V = gamma_U M U/(m + gamma_U M). The shift is -4.56e-4 at m/M = 1e-3 and -4.57e-7 at 1e-6, and is zero to double precision at spacecraft/BH ratios (rederive I). Negligible, but it is an unstated hypothesis.

WEAKENED, arrival.py:9, 110-111 ('Free', 'costs nothing'): no propellant is spent, but full reversal needs a fine-tuned impact parameter. At v_inf = 0.35 c around Schwarzschild, chi = pi needs b = 13.1783 M, only 9.4% above the capture threshold b_crit = 12.0476 M, with periapsis 5.604 M. d(chi)/db = -0.984 rad/M, so holding chi within 0.01 rad needs b held to about 0.0102 M (rederive H). 'Costs nothing' holds for propellant only. The navigation and timing precision are unpriced, which the tree itself records as OPEN at shipspec.py 'timing precision required'.

It tests the code's sign flip, not time symmetry. The physical check, that incoming w = 2U/(1+U^2) with the deflector receding at U ends at exactly 0, is supplied in rederive C and passes symbolically. Recorded, not repaired.

rederivation.outcome: OVERALL PASS (output in rederive/sr-velocity-addition-slingshot-strong-field.out). A: symbolic full reversal from rest gives v_f = 2U/(1+U^2) exactly; 0.623608018 at U = 0.35, which matches arrival.py:79. B: head-on rapidity gain = 2 artanh U for every incoming w (max deviation 4.6e-14 over a 6x5 grid); tail-on theta_f = 2 artanh U - theta_w (2.9e-15). C: exact time reverse (w = 2U/(1+U^2), deflector receding at U) gives final speed 0 identically in sympy, so the tree's 'takes back exactly' is TRUE in that configuration. D: with w = 0.866, U = 0.35 the speed change is -0.3390, not -0.6236; with w = 0.8, U = 0.2 it is -0.2000, not -0.3846, so the velocity-change reading fails off the reverse configuration. E: a 2D scan over entry and exit angles never exceeds the full-reversal head-on value, which confirms it is the ceiling (0.623608018, 0.613793103, 0.897996787). F: shedding 0.866 c takes 1.802 passes at 0.35 c and 3.248 at 0.2 c; a single-pass deflector needs 0.577316 c. G: Zhang's 50% = (1+U)/(1-U) at U = 0.2 exactly, and from rest the ceiling is 8.33%. H: in Schwarzschild at v_inf = 0.35, deflection pi is reached at b = 13.17827 M (b_crit = 12.04760 M) with periapsis 5.6038 M > 2M, while the weak field (b = 40 M) gives only 0.52 rad. The large-b limit matches 2(1+v^2)/(v^2 b) to 4e-5. I: finite-mass correction is O(m/M).

later_literature.ref: J. F. Acevedo & A. Ritz, 'Binary-boosted Dark Matter', arXiv:2603.08781v1 (2026)
later_literature.what: Confirms the geometry of the maximum: 'maximal energy gain is 2 u_M2 v_i, which occurs when beta = 0 and chi = 180 deg', i.e. head-on full reversal, the Newtonian analogue of 2U/(1+U^2). It restricts the formula to the restricted 3-body problem with the heavy component effectively at rest and a single two-body hyperbolic encounter in the secondary's frame. For compact equal-mass BH binaries they 'numerically observed ejections that exceed this estimate by an order unity factor' because spheres of influence overlap. The single-encounter law is therefore neither exact nor a ceiling inside a compact binary, which is where arrival.py puts the destination deflector.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. Evidence AGAINST 'the authors lacked data' changing it: the result is pure special-relativistic kinematics (Lorentz velocity addition applied to a speed-conserving scatter). It has no empirical input except c, which is exact by definition, and it is re-derived symbolically here (checks A-C). No datum has moved and none can move it. Evidence FOR a gap, of a different kind: what the tree's use lacks is not data but three hypotheses. (1) The incoming speed must equal the departure gain for 'takes back exactly' to hold as a velocity statement; in general only rapidity is additive. (2) The deflector must be isolated and unaccelerated; the one later paper that tested the single-encounter formula inside compact BH binaries (Acevedo & Ritz 2026, numerical three-body runs, data Zhang 2020 did not have) finds order-unity departures from it. (3) Steering precision: b must be held to about 0.01 M near 1.09 b_crit. Having (2) narrows where the formula may be applied. It does not overturn the kinematics.
grade_evidence: The kinematics STANDS: 2U/(1+U^2) is exactly the full-reversal gain from rest (sympy, check A), it is the ceiling over all geometries (check E), and the exact time reverse ends at rest identically (check C). Deflection pi is attainable outside the horizon at finite b (check H), so the strong-field limit is physically reachable. The TREE'S USE is broader than the result. (a) The receding-pass statement 'the same magnitude negative' holds as a velocity change only for incoming speed 2U/(1+U^2); at w = 0.866, U = 0.35 the loss is 0.339, not 0.624 (check D). (b) Braking the tree's 0.866 c needs 1.80 to 3.25 passes at U = 0.35-0.2 c, or a single deflector at 0.577 c (check F), and arrival.py:160 does not state this. (c) The isolated, unaccelerated deflector and test-particle hypotheses are never named. In a compact binary the single-encounter law departs by an order-unity factor (Acevedo & Ritz 2026, READ). (d) 'Costs nothing' prices propellant only, while steering needs |db| ~ 0.01 M (check H). (e) The selftest time-symmetry row (arrival.py:80-81) is hollow. None of these is a computed contradiction of a statement the tree actually evaluates, because its only numeric use is the exact reverse configuration, so the grade is not WRONG. Separately, a cross-key DISCREPANCY is recorded, not graded here: the 50%/pass-from-gamma0=1 ladder behind the 0.866 c (THE-ENGINE.md:116, slingshot.py:55) exceeds the full-reversal kinematic ceiling this key establishes (check G).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restricts the claim to the exact reverse configuration (incoming speed = 2U/(1+U^2), or the rapidity form theta -> theta - 2 artanh U per pass), names the isolated/unaccelerated-deflector and test-particle hypotheses, and states the pass count for 0.866 c. To WRONG: a consumer that numerically applies -2U/(1+U^2) as the velocity change for an incoming speed other than 2U/(1+U^2). No such call site was found in arrival.py; its only call is the selftest. To OPEN on the external side: reading Zhang Sec. 3 (pp.4-12), not available this run, would show whether his relativistic slingshot formulae carry further hypotheses (e.g. a straight-line BH trajectory during the encounter). That reading could add drift items but cannot move the kinematics.
